claim: In-row spacing follows travel: 4-cell maize plate at ratio 1.0 gives 236 mm nominal for the 250 mm target, about 220 to 240 mm with the 1.2 to 1.7 % skid and up to 6.7 % shorter rolling radius, so spacing is calibrated per seedbed
law: Spacing = pi D / (cells x ratio); D = 300 mm over the lug tips
check: claimed 236 mm, estimate 236 mm (ratio 1.00)

claim: The 76-link #35 chain fits the 286 mm sprocket centres, the spring tensioner taking up the slack
law: Chain length L/p = 2C/p + (T1 + T2)/2 + ((T2 - T1)/2 pi)^2 p/C; idler deflection sqrt(slack C / 2) within the tensioner's 45 mm
check: 35 mm idler deflection <= 45 mm idler deflection

claim: Meter torque at the plate shaft stays under the 1.0 N m design value
law: Janssen wall pressure of a 0.2 m seed head on the lower quarter of the plate, friction 0.4; brush drag; bearings and chain 0.1 N m
check: 0.2 N m <= 1 N m

claim: Chain tension at the design meter torque with a 1.2 service factor is far below the #35 chain's minimum tensile strength
law: T = torque / pitch radius; #35 roller chain minimum tensile strength about 7.8 kN (ANSI B29.1 class)
check: 52 N (limit is 10 % of the minimum tensile strength) <= 780 N (limit is 10 % of the minimum tensile strength)

claim: Wheel skid from the meter torque stays under 8 %, so spacing follows travel
law: Traction ratio = drive force / wheel load; Brixius traction relation for a rigid wheel in a cone index of 100 to 300 kPa

claim: Each maize cell fills with one seed at 0.299 m/s cell speed (walking-speed rule 2.9 km/h)
law: Gravity fill of a cell passing a seed pool; the assumed 0.30 m/s working limit for vertical cell plates is not from a cited test; the kinematic indicator for a still seed (the seed falls its own depth while the open cell passes) is 0.20 m/s
check: 0.299 m/s against an assumed 0.30 m/s, no margin; a seed dragged by the plate fills at higher speed than a still seed

claim: Spacing coefficient of variation of 31 % of all spacings, design case (target 30 %)
law: Monte Carlo of 20,000 cells with an assumed 5 % miss, 4 % double, 15 mm drop scatter and 5 +/- 1.5 % slip; the result is set by the assumed miss and double rates, which only a bench test gives
check: 31 % of all spacings, 9 % for singles, against 30 %; within the uncertainty of the assumed inputs

claim: Horizontal component of the push in the design case is 150 N or less (the push applied along the 50 deg handle is 205 N, 157 N of it downward)
law: Planar statics with Brixius motion resistance (used outside its calibrated range for small rigid wheels), opener draft from an assumed 30 kPa specific resistance (68 of the 133 N)

claim: One operator sustains the push: 132 N horizontal (205 N along the handle) at 0.81 m/s is 106 W of external work while walking, with a 15 s turn every 62 s
law: Sustained pushing guidance (ISO 11228-2 method) depends on distance, frequency, height and the population; not yet assessed. The kit's screening value for sustained cranking is 75 W
check: 106 W external against a 75 W cranking screen; walking push uses larger muscle groups; ISO 11228-2 assessment to do

claim: Seeder with the marker kit weighs 15 kg or less
law: Mass build-up from the model's part volumes (steel 7,850 kg/m3, PETG 1,270 kg/m3, aluminium 2,700 kg/m3), every fastener from the model, and about 4.5 kg of catalogue-class bought parts whose 5 % error is about 0.2 kg

claim: Side rails stay below yield with a dynamic factor of 3 for drops and stones
law: Beam bending of 25 x 25 x 1.5 square tube, S235 yield 235 MPa (EN 10025-2)
check: 70 MPa (limit is yield / 1.5) <= 156.7 MPa (limit is yield / 1.5)

claim: Handle side tube (22 x 1.2) stays below yield under a 100 N side load at the grip together with the heavy-seedbed push (221 N at 36 deg)
law: Cantilever bending of round tube in two planes, combined; S235 yield 235 MPa (independent review of 2026-10-24 added the push component)
check: 143 MPa (limit is yield / 1.5) <= 156.7 MPa (limit is yield / 1.5)
closed_by: SDL-CAL-001 section 7 (fatigue to test at TRL 4)

claim: A seed in a cell is not thrown out of the cell by the plate's rotation
law: Centripetal acceleration omega^2 r at the cell circle against g

claim: Field capacity 0.142 ha/h (7.1 h/ha) for maize on 0.75 m rows at 2.9 km/h
law: Capacity = row spacing x speed x field efficiency (65 %: 50 m rows, 15 s turns, 90 s refills, 85 % working time)
check: claimed 0.142 ha/h, estimate 0.141 ha/h (ratio 1.00)

claim: One 2.42 L hopper fill sows about 1,450 m of maize row at 250 mm
law: Row length = volume x bulk density (0.72 kg/L) / seed mass (0.30 g) x spacing
check: claimed 1451 m, estimate 1.45e+03 m (ratio 1.00)

claim: The 10 mm groundnut plate, the slowest, prints in 2 h or less
law: Print time = deposited volume / 6 mm3/s average rate (unsourced; 1.6 mm skins, 1.2 mm walls round the rim, every cell and the bore, 20 % infill since SDL-DEC-001 F8). With the cell ends left out and 25 % infill it read 1.96 h; corrected it was 2.05 h, a fail, fixed by F8

claim: A desktop FDM print holds the cell size closely enough: +/-0.2 mm on the pelleted carrot cell (3.8 mm deep for a 3.3 mm pellet)
law: Tolerance ratio 0.2 / 3.8 mm = 5.3 % of the cell, but 43 % of its 0.47 mm clearance over the pellet; FDM holes and slots print undersize (a bias, not only a tolerance)
check: 5.3 % of the cell against the 10 % rule; tight against the clearance; a printed test coupon of cells sets the offset

claim: A drive-wheel bump moves the opener by 0.69 of the bump, so +/-10 mm depth holds for bumps up to about +/-14.5 mm (ploughed seedbed)
law: Rigid frame on two wheels: the opener point, 181 mm behind the drive axle on a 580 mm wheelbase, moves (x - x_press) / wheelbase of a drive wheel rise
check: 0.69 of a drive-wheel rise <= 1 of a drive-wheel rise

claim: Printed PETG plate takes the drive at its D-flat without yielding
law: Bearing stress = torque x 1.2 / (lever arm x flat area); PETG tensile yield about 50 MPa (typical datasheet value)
check: 5.7 MPa (limit is yield / 3 for a printed part) <= 16.67 MPa (limit is yield / 3 for a printed part)

claim: PETG plates degrade in strong sun; ASA is used where plates stay in the sun, PLA for trials only
law: UV photo-oxidation of polyesters; ASA's acrylic outer phase is UV stable (polymer supplier datasheets)
check: Material rule decided (SDL-DDR-001 item 9); plates inspected each season (PRC Safety)

claim: Treated seed is toxic; gloves, no eating or drinking while filling, cleaning outdoors and a hopper never used for food control the exposure
law: Seed treatment labels and humanitarian guidance require PPE, especially gloves (ICRC, Warning: treated seeds)
check: Safety claim only; the design adds no exposure route beyond filling and cleaning

claim: Maize sown at 50 mm sits within the recommended seeding depth
law: Purdue University Department of Agronomy (2022): most common recommended corn seeding depths are 1.5 to 2 inches (38 to 51 mm); the design case sits at the top of the range and +/-10 mm control spans 40 to 60 mm
check: 50 mm <= 51 mm
closed_by: Purdue Agronomy (2022); depth set per crop on the shank

claim: Even spacing raises yield: about 140 to 160 kg/ha of maize per 25 mm less spacing standard deviation, less at smallholder yield levels
law: Nielsen, Purdue University plant spacing trials
check: Cited effect; SeedLine claims only that spacing follows travel, not a yield figure

claim: The housing door's two thumb screws land in solid housing wall
law: Fit check in the detailed model: as drawn at kit 1.7 the screws at 12 mm from the door's rear edge stood over the 128 x 132 opening, not over wall
check: Fixed: door 146 x 150 to the housing's edges; screws at 7 mm from the rear edge (rear wall band) and 7 mm up (floor band), into M4 heat-set inserts
closed_by: SDL-DEC-001 F1 (decided under the standing instruction of 2026-10-23)

claim: The wheel hub cross bolt clears the wheel's disc web
law: Fit check in the detailed model: the cross hole at 107 mm put the bolt head and nut in the plane of the 2 mm web
check: Fixed: cross hole moved to 122 mm from the axle's chain-side end, 15 mm off the web, inside the 45 mm hub
closed_by: SDL-DEC-001 F2 (decided under the standing instruction of 2026-10-23)

claim: The tensioner's pivot fixing clears the chain's upper strand
law: Fit check in the detailed model: a head or nut on the boss's outer end sits in the upper strand (7 mm above the pivot) at the real 12 mm chain width
check: Fixed: M8 x 40 screw from inside the frame through the rail into the tensioner's tapped boss
closed_by: SDL-DEC-001 F3 (decided under the standing instruction of 2026-10-23)

claim: A jammed plate does not damage the steel drive: the wheel drives until it skids (about 11 N m at the plate shaft), and the printed plate's bore strips first
law: Traction about 0.7 of the drive-wheel load at 150 mm; chain tension against 7.8 kN; D-flat bearing stress against about 50 MPa for PETG (independent review of 2026-10-24)
check: 497 N chain tension (limit 10 % of minimum tensile); the plate's D-flat reaches about 54 MPa, so the plate is the sacrificial part <= 780 N chain tension (limit 10 % of minimum tensile); the plate's D-flat reaches about 54 MPa, so the plate is the sacrificial part
closed_by: SDL-CAL-001 section 7; spare plate in the kit

claim: The tensioner takes up chain wear until about 0.8 % elongation; the chain is then shortened by a link pair or replaced
law: Idler deflection sqrt(slack x C / 2): 35 mm new, 48 mm at 1 % elongation, against 45 mm of take-up (independent review of 2026-10-24)
check: 45 mm take-up against mm needed at 1 % elongation (the claim is the wear limit) <= 48 mm take-up against mm needed at 1 % elongation (the claim is the wear limit)
closed_by: SDL-BLD-001 first checks; wear limit in the build plan

claim: The 20 x 2 mm hopper uprights carry the hopper sideways: they sway 1 mm before the hopper's neck bears in the housing collar, which takes the rest
law: Cantilever deflection F L^3 / 3 E I limited to the collar's 1 mm clearance (SDL-DDR-003 P7); free-standing they would reach about 300 MPa at three times the full hopper's weight sideways (independent review of 2026-10-24)
check: 10 MPa at 1 mm sway (limit yield / 1.5) <= 156.7 MPa at 1 mm sway (limit yield / 1.5)

claim: The aluminium marker arm stays below yield at its full 900 mm reach with a dynamic factor of 3
law: Cantilever bending of 20 x 1.5 tube under 20 N side drag; 6061-T6 tube, typical minimum yield about 240 MPa (6063-T6 about 170 MPa would give a factor of 1.3); independent review of 2026-10-24
check: 128 MPa (limit is yield / 1.5) <= 160 MPa (limit is yield / 1.5)

claim: The hopper's M5 heat-set inserts fit their bosses
law: Insert makers specify a hole of about 6.4 mm for M5 heat-set inserts; the bosses were drawn with 4.0 mm holes (a tap drill size)
check: Fixed: 6.5 mm holes in the eight bosses
closed_by: SDL-DEC-001 F4 (decided under the standing instruction of 2026-10-23)

claim: Option B: six punches on a 480 mm rim give 251 mm spacing
law: Spacing = 2 pi R / N (rim rolling on the surface; sinkage shortens it)
check: claimed 251 mm, estimate 251 mm (ratio 1.00)

claim: Option B: the wheel's weight presses a punch 50 mm into tilled soil (32 N needed at a 200 kPa cone index)
law: Penetration force about cone index x punch section; wheel share of a 12.4 kg machine about 75 %

claim: Option B is limited to tilled seedbeds, as option A is: in firm untilled soil (1.5 MPa cone index) a punch needs about 243 N, more than the wheel's share plus 100 N of downward push; the crossover is near 1.2 MPa
law: As OB2; firm untilled soils reach cone indexes of 1 to 2 MPa (typical range, to confirm with partner data). The claim is the limitation, so the check is that the force needed exceeds the force available
check: 243 N needed against N available >= 191 N needed against N available

claim: Option B: a seed released at -15 deg reaches the punch's jaws before the jaw opens at the bottom (arrives at -78 deg; the punch enters the soil at -54 deg; at about 3.3 km/h it arrives after 90 deg)
law: Seed sliding out along a rotating tube: gravity, centrifugal and Coriolis terms with wall friction 0.4, at 2.9 km/h
check: 78 deg past forward (the jaw opens near 90) <= 90 deg past forward (the jaw opens near 90)

claim: Option B: the hub cell ring's cells move at 0.23 m/s, under the 0.30 m/s fill limit assumed for option A
law: Cell speed = wheel angular speed x cell radius (69 mm)

claim: Option B: soil pushes the trailing jaw open in the soil and a torsion spring closes it as the punch lifts out
law: Punch planters with hinged jaws are established (jab planters; Molin et al. 1998 report a punch planter prototype with synchronisation and soil-sticking problems)
check: Working in principle; jaw opening timing, soil sticking and spring force not calculated
